must_fix: Abstract/Table 1 lead with pooled ΔECE=0.113 (n=60 cells at s=1.5, none) from results/exp04_main_h1.json. Independently recomputing that grid, sklearn sets (breast_cancer+wine, n=30) have mean ΔECE=0.042 (25/30 positive) while synthetic sets (n=30) have mean ΔECE=0.184 (26/30 positive). Pooled accuracy drop is −0.156 and ΔBrier=0.257; synthetic logreg alone is ΔECE=0.292 with accuracy 0.932→0.620. The headline number is a synthetic accuracy-collapse mixture, not a typical tabular effect. Report the real-vs-synthetic (or 12 cell-mean) split in the abstract/table, not only the n=60 pool.

paper/main.tex Results §2 splices two different calibrators: 'Wine random forests benefit from isotonic (NumWineRfIsoHelp=−0.123 ECE; shifted ECE NumWineRfNoneSh=0.175 → temperature NumWineRfTempSh=0.068)'. From exp04, isotonic help is ECE_sh(iso)−ECE_sh(none)=0.052−0.175=−0.123, but 0.175→0.068 is the temperature path (ECE_sh(temp)=0.068). Isotonic shifted ECE is 0.052, not 0.068. Fix the parenthetical so the named calibrator matches the JSON fields.

Quantile-slice cell-mean ΔECE=0.016 (sd 0.006) is n=6 dataset×model means on breast_cancer+synthetic_shift only (results/exp05_ablate_shift_family.json; wine and synthetic_multiclass absent). The paper contrasts it with pooled feature-perturbation 0.113 from the 4×3×5 grid. On the same 6 cells, gaussian s=1.5 none cell-mean ΔECE is 0.105, not 0.113. Label n=6 / two datasets in that sentence, and compare to the matched gaussian cells.

The selection vs perturbation contrast is not strength-matched. Gaussian s=1.5 on columns [0,1,2,3] (src/calibshift/shift.py: X[:,cols]+=s*X.std(axis=0)[cols], y frozen) drops pooled accuracy by 0.156. Quantile-slice (median of feature 0, pairs kept) drops accuracy by only ~0.01–0.03 and halves n_test (breast_cancer 143→72). 'Order of magnitude smaller ΔECE' is therefore confounded with a much milder intervention; do not attribute the 0.016 vs 0.113 gap solely to preserving P(Y|X).

Methods (paper/main.tex) say ECE is biased and 'we therefore also report Brier score and NLL'. Code in src/calibshift/metrics.py and runner.py does compute them (exp04 none s=1.5: mean ΔBrier=0.257, ΔNLL=0.792). The results table/figures are ECE-only. Either show Brier/NLL/accuracy next to Table 1 or drop the claim that those scores are the robustness check.
weaknesses: ΔECE = ECE_shift−ECE_iid is a poor summary of whether maps help under shift. At s=1.5 pooled, maps cut iid ECE (none 0.053 → temperature 0.031, isotonic 0.023) while barely moving shifted ECE (none 0.166 → temperature 0.155, isotonic 0.164, histogram 0.166). Table 1 therefore shows larger ΔECE after mapping (0.124/0.141/0.141 vs 0.113) mostly because the iid baseline improved. Temperature actually lowers shifted ECE vs none by 0.012 on average (33/60 help, 27/60 hurt). The paper's separate 'help' figure is the right estimand; Table 1 is easy to misread as 'maps make shift worse'.

12/12 seed-averaged means are positive, but breast_cancer×HGB is 0.002±0.009 with seed signs 2+/3− (seeds 1,2,3 negative in exp04). breast_cancer×logreg is 3+/2− (mean 0.028). The Wilcoxon p=2.4e-04 on 12 means is 1/2^12 given all-positive ranks, not independent dataset evidence. Paper flags pseudo-replication for n=60; the 12/12 sentence in the abstract still oversells homogeneity.

exp07 is not a noise-feature control on breast_cancer. Trailing columns [26,27,28,29] are 'worst' morphology features. Independent recompute: breast_cancer HGB trailing ΔECE=0.072 vs first-four 0.002; logreg trailing 0.058 vs 0.028. The paper only reports synthetic_shift RF 0.009 vs 0.041 (matches JSON). Omitting the breast_cancer trailing-column cells lets a 'shift of used covariates' reading look cleaner than the full ablation.

H3 'oracle' in src/calibshift/runner.py is oracle_density_ratio_1d(X_cal[:,0], X_shift[:,0]) — a 1-D histogram ratio on feature 0, not p_test(x)/p_cal(x). In exp03 the 4 shifted columns are rng.choice (n_features=4); at s=1.5 feature 0 is never among them (0/6 cells). That is why analysis.md's 0.744 vs 0.747 is a null comparison: weights are estimated on an unshifted coordinate. Paper correctly kills H3 and calls the estimator misspecified; leftover 'oracle' naming is still too strong. In exp04 (cols fixed to [0,1,2,3]) the same 1-D weights often *hurt* coverage (breast_cancer logreg none s=1.5: unweighted 0.778 vs weighted 0.673).

Wine test n=45 with 15 equal-width ECE bins (n_cal=44, n_train=89). The Niculescu-Mizil-style sanity (wine RF iid ECE 0.147±0.020) and wine RF 'help' numbers sit on ~3 observations per bin if confidence were uniform, and many bins are empty. Disclosed, but those cells should not be pooled equally with synthetic n_test=500.

Quantile-slice ΔECE is ECE(subset)−ECE(full test), not a paired same-n comparison; importance_resample draws with replacement (duplicates enter ECE). Fallback in quantile_slice (keep all if <10 points) did not fire in exp05 (0 cells). Pairs are preserved (X[mask],y[mask] and X[idx],y[idx] in shift.py) — the design issue is estimand/n, not pair-breaking.

Conformal quantile is computed on the same calibration split used to fit T / isotonic / histogram (runner.py cal.fit(p_cal_raw, y_cal) then split_conformal_quantile(y_cal, p_cal)). For calibrator='none' this is valid split conformal; headline coverage is logreg/none so it is not leaked. Any coverage numbers with temperature/isotonic/histogram are not finite-sample valid.

gaussian_feature_shift uses test-split feature sd (X.std on the matrix being shifted), as the paper states. Not train/cal leakage, but strength is test-sample-dependent. Module docstring in src/calibshift/shift.py still titles these 'Covariate-shift mechanisms'; exp05/run.py says 'alternative covariate-shift mechanisms'. The paper text got the naming right; the code comments did not.

Temperature is softmax(log p / T) on clipped probabilities, not Guo logit temperature (disclosed). Multiclass isotonic/histogram map confidence, not Dirichlet (disclosed). Histogram empty bins are filled with (lo+hi)/2, which can inject 0.5 into unseen confidence bins under shift (not disclosed).

Cited well-known keys in paper/main.tex (guo2017calibration, ovadia2019trust, niculescumizil2005probabilities, tibshirani2019covariate, brier1950verification, gneiting2007scoring, naeini2015bbq, nixon2019measuring, kumar2019verified, kull2019dirichlet, grinsztajn2022trees, angelopoulos2021gentle, pampari2020unsupervised/arXiv:2006.16405, silvafilho2021survey/arXiv:2112.10327, wang2023survey/arXiv:2308.01222) match real papers. vovk2005algorithmic is the 2005 book cited as @article — metadata slop, not an invented paper. Unused macro NumWineLogregAcc is harmless.
strengths: Mechanism naming in title/abstract/H1/limitations matches the code: gaussian_feature_shift copies X, adds s*σ̂_j on listed columns, and returns the original y (shift.py:32–34). That is frozen-label feature perturbation / a change in P(Y|X) at the observed x, not covariate shift. The paper says so repeatedly and withdraws the original CS wording. That is the correct scientific move.

Selection operators preserve (X,y) pairs: quantile_slice returns X[mask], y[mask]; importance_resample returns X[idx], y[idx]. No label shuffling. The paper's 'closer to covariate shift' control is implemented as claimed, even if it is a weak shift.

Split hygiene is clean for the headline protocol. runner.py: 50% train / 50% of remainder cal / 50% test, stratified, random_state=seed and seed+1. Model.fit on train only; calibrators fit only on (p_cal_raw, y_cal); shift applied only to X_test. Calibration data never includes the test set. exp04: n_shifted==n_test on all 240 gaussian cells.

Conformal score in src/calibshift/conformal.py is LAC / 1−p_y (scores=1-p[i,y_i]; coverage scores<=q_hat), explicitly not APS. Paper methods match (α=0.1, 15-bin confidence ECE). Coverage at s=0 for breast_cancer logreg none is 0.913; at s=1.5/2.5 it is 0.778/0.608 — same numbers as NumBcLogregCovSZero/OneFive/TwoFive.

All 57 macros in paper/numbers.tex independently recomputed from results/exp04_main_h1.json, exp05_ablate_shift_family.json, exp07_noise_feature_control.json, summary_main.json, and stats_tests.json: 0 mismatches. Headlines that trace: n_ok=240, failed=0, none ΔECE mean/std 0.113/0.149, 51/9 of 60, temperature 0.124/0.150 56/4, isotonic 0.141 53/7, histogram 0.141 57/3, Wilcoxon p 2.2e-10 / 3.1e-11 / 4.6e-11 / 3.3e-11, 12/12 means p=2.4e-04, bc logreg acc/ECE 0.979/0.032±0.010, wine RF iid ECE 0.147±0.020, bc HGB ΔECE 0.002±0.009, synth logreg ΔECE 0.292±0.214, coverage 0.913/0.778/0.608 and synth 0.634, wine RF iso help −0.123, bc logreg iso help +0.074, wine RF none/temp shifted ECE 0.175/0.068, quantile 0.016±0.006, importance 0.011±0.031, trailing synth RF 0.009 vs first-four 0.041, synth logreg acc 0.932→0.620, NumNTests=21, NumEceBins=15, NumAlpha=0.1, NumNSeeds=5. Results look code-written (schema calibshift.result.v1, sort_keys envelopes), not hand-edited.

Primary claim is appropriately weakened relative to the selection-shift control: the paper does not claim i.i.d. post-hoc maps fail under covariate shift, reports the HGB exception, and records killed H2/H3. analysis.md licensed claims match the abstract. Paired ΔECE on the same test rows for feature perturbation is the right design for that mechanism.

Limitations section is unusually specific (frozen labels ≠ CS; wine n~45; temperature-on-probabilities; 1-D H3 weights; unadjusted 21 tests; novelty scoped to verified.bib's 47 entries, which matches the bib file count).
